turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Morning. In you come, out of that rain. Did you find a parking space at all?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Good morning, doctor. Thank you. I did, after circling twice. The traffic at the canal bridge was terribly slow today.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): The lights are out on that junction again. I was stuck coming from Rathmines myself.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): It is the same most Tuesdays. My daughter told me the bus was packed as well. I am sorry I am a few minutes late.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Not at all. The weather has the whole place crawling. Sit down there. What can I do for you?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): It is the spring trouble, doctor. I sneeze a great deal, my eyes itch, and my nose runs.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Every spring. How many years has that been going on?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Five or six years, since we moved out to the suburbs. It arrives when the trees do.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): And this season, when did it come back?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): About three weeks ago. The sneezing started first, mostly in the mornings, same as every spring. It eases when I get to work, but it never quite stops.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Both eyes itching, or just the one?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Both eyes, these same three weeks. They itch, and they water a little as well.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): The nose, is it clear or coloured?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Clear. It is not coloured, and it has run the same three weeks.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any cough with this?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): A sore throat?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Not really.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Fever, or chills?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I feel well in myself otherwise.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Now, you have asthma on the file. Still the case?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. I have asthma, diagnosed about ten years ago. It has been quiet, thankfully.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): What inhalers are you on for it?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Only salbutamol, the blue one. Two puffs when I need them. No preventer at present.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any wheeze with this spell?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Never. Not with this.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Chest pain?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Palpitations?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Not that either.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Are you short of breath?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): No... well, sometimes, if I am rushing for the train.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): So only on rushing. Not while you are at rest.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): That is correct. Not at rest.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Grand. And for the nose and the eyes, are you on a tablet?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): I take ceterizine, ten milligrams. The box says one a day.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Cetirizine. Do you manage it every day, as the box says?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really every day.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): umm, let me think. If it is hit and miss, the eyes often lag behind. Does it make you drowsy at all?
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, a small bit drowsy, if I take it in the morning before work.
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): That is a known nuisance with cetirizine. Any allergies to medicines?
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): No. None.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): Family history, anyone else with allergies?
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): My sister is allergic to dust. She has been for years. I was at the hurling with her husband in Thurles on Sunday, extra time, pouring rain.
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): Thurles, were you. Who came out on top?

[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Tipperary, by two points. He was utterly delighted. We did not get in the door until near midnight, and the road was completely choked. A grand match, though, if you like the wet.
[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): I do, in fairness. uh, there is nothing like it. Anyway, enough of that, back to you. Let me look at the eyes and the nose, and listen in.
[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): Both conjunctivae are a little red, no swelling of the lids. Nasal lining is pale and boggy. Chest is clear, no wheeze to hear.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): That matches how it feels, doctor. The breathing is all right once I am sitting.

[SEG0050] person_1 (DOCTOR): Thinking it out loud, the pollen sets off histamine in the lining of the nose and the eyes, and that is the itch and the running. My working impression is seasonal allergic rhinitis, hay fever, with your asthma quiet behind it. I would not call it an infection.

[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): err, the plan then. We will stop the cetirizine, because you only take it sometimes and it sedates you. I am switching you to fexofenadine, 120 milligrams, one tablet once a day. And olopatadine drops, one drop in each eye twice a day.

[SEG0052] person_1 (DOCTOR): Carry on with the salbutamol exactly as you do now. Keep the windows shut on high pollen days, and have a shower when you come in from the garden. I will have reception book you back in six weeks.
[SEG0053] person_2 (PATIENT): Six weeks suits me very well. Thank you, doctor. I appreciate you explaining it, and I shall follow what you have said.

spec.situation: Sneezing, itchy eyes and runny nose every spring; takes cetirizine 'sometimes'; sister is allergic to dust; no wheeze; doctor changes antihistamine and adds eye drops.

traps.happens: The patient denies some symptoms (said as 'no', 'not really', 'never'), has a chronic condition named earlier (for example asthma or hypertension) and later the doctor asks about another symptom of it, and one answer is a double negative or a correction ('not that either', 'no... well, sometimes').
traps.label_rule: Denials go in negative_findings with the exact thing denied, never in symptoms. NEVER write a negative about a condition the patient has said they have. A corrected answer keeps only the final version. A negative is never a symptom, and 'not painful' is the finding 'pain' absent, not a symptom called 'painless'.

features: tangent_small_talk: a long tangent or small talk (traffic, cricket, the weather, a grandchild) that holds NO clinical content; nothing from it is extracted.
ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.

bad.reason: Patient said 'Not really,' not a definite denial of sore throat.
Transcript only denies allergies to medicines, not all allergies.

omissions.text: Nasal discharge was described as clear for the same three-week duration, not just negative for coloured discharge.
Patient reported feeling otherwise well in themselves.
Asthma was described as quiet/stable currently.
Patient stated there is no preventer inhaler at present.
Medicine allergy history was specifically negative for allergies to medicines, not allergies in general.
Chest examination included that the chest was clear, not only that no wheeze was heard.
